title: Ordered affine integration orientations and zero-section identities
statement: Fix a finite purity datum P [def-pur-conventions] and d,e in N. For an affine finite-type k-scheme B let A^r_B be the fixed finite-coordinate affine model, with projection P_r and zero section z_r [def-sbc-affine-space, def-asd-vector-bundle-zero-section]. Use the canonical coordinate, unit, site and Tate comparisons of [def-pur-composition-model-orientation-coordinates]. There exists a family G_r:T_r -> omega_(P_r) of isomorphisms satisfying the prescribed ordered-Gamma normalization and its rank-zero identity. For every B, sigma_(q,P_e) followed by the inverse total G equals the tensor of the base-changed inverse rank-d G and the pulled-back inverse rank-e G, followed by mu. Its zero-section pullback b_r satisfies nu_(d,e) followed by b_(d+e) = (b_d tensor b_e) followed by ordered Tate concatenation. For every composable pair f:U->V, g:V->T of separated finite-type smooth morphisms of pure ranks d,e between affine finite-type k-schemes, the three normal orientations beta_f, f*beta_g and beta_(gf) agree with b_d,b_e,b_(d+e) under every prescribed compatible conormal frame, including its fixed standard-section base-change comparison.

proof.text:
For a trivial bundle $u$ of rank $r$ over a separated finite-type base write $P_{u,H}$ for the integration-transposed map, and $G_u=P_{u,\Lambda}$. The ordered-integration theorem gives $P_{u,H}=\Gamma_{u,H}$ at every $n\geq1$; the coefficient-counit normalization gives
$$\Gamma_{u,H}=\theta_{u,H}(1\otimes G_u).$$
Both statements use the same inverse projection, restricted projective-line trace and actual exceptional adjunction as in the question. Thus this equality identifies actual maps, not just objects. Its inputs include the pulled-back Tate lines, $\omega_{P_e}$ and the coefficient-unit object: the coefficient normalization supplies the finite-Tor etale witnesses and invertible projection maps, and the tensor-mate statement supplies $\omega_{P_e}\in D^b_{ctf}$. The model agreement theorem identifies the inverse of $G_u$ with the specified diagonal orientation. In particular all $G_u$ used below are isomorphisms, and this argument does not impose $e(E/\mathbf Q_\ell)\mid n$.

source.place: Step 1: affine model and compatibility of the diagonal orientations

proof.text:
Apply integration-normalized direct-sum compatibility to the two trivial bundles of ranks $d,e$ over the affine finite-type scheme $B$, with $f=q$, $g=P_e$, $h=P_{d+e}$ and $K=\Lambda_B$. Its source identification is $\mu^{-1}$ from Step 1. Its $q$-orientation is the base change along $P_e$ of the rank-$d$ unit orientation, as required in the statement; by the base-change clause of the same theorem (exchange $e$ and associator $a$, at $K=\Lambda_B$) this base change is the integration-normalized map of the trivial rank-$d$ bundle $q$ itself, i.e. $G_q$ of Step 2, so the factor $\gamma_q$ at $\omega_g$ is $\theta_{q,\omega_g}(1\otimes G_q)$. This compatibility is initially ordinary-etale. The vector-integration comparison identifies its traces, projection maps and exceptional transposes with the specified pro-etale ones. The compact-support site-coherence equation identifies its compositor with the actual pro-etale compositor; conjugating this equation by the composite Hom bijections identifies the right mates by mate pasting. Thus on this site the direct-sum formula is
$$G_h=c^{-1}\Gamma_{q,\omega_g}(Lq^*G_g\otimes1)\mu^{-1}.$$
The bases here are affine finite type (and therefore in the separated finite-type domain of Step 2), all coefficient inputs have its finite-Tor witnesses, and every comparison in the formula is the prescribed one.

source.place: Step 1: affine model and compatibility of the diagonal orientations

proof.text:
Substitute Step 2 into the formula of Step 3 and use naturality of $\theta_{q,-}$ in $G_g:T_e\to\omega_g$. With the tensor symmetry displayed in the definition of $\sigma$ this gives
$$G_h\mu=c^{-1}\theta_{q,\omega_g}\mathrm{sym}(G_q\otimes Lq^*G_g)=\sigma_{q,P_e}(G_q\otimes Lq^*G_g).$$
Compose on the left by $G_h^{-1}$ and on the right by $G_q^{-1}\otimes Lq^*G_g^{-1}$. The result is exactly
$$\Gamma_{P_{d+e},\Lambda}^{-1}\sigma_{q,P_e}=\mu(\Gamma_{q,\Lambda}^{-1}\otimes Lq^*\Gamma_{P_e,\Lambda}^{-1}).$$
This is an equality of the integration-normalized maps. No choice of a trivialization of the target line enters the cancellation. For $d=0$ or $e=0$, ordered comparisons are identities at rank zero, the composite-adjunction mate is the identity comparison, and the same calculation reduces to a tensor-unit law.

source.place: Step 1: affine model and compatibility of the diagonal orientations

proof.text:
Pull Step 4 back along the total zero section $z_{d+e}:B\to\mathbf A^{d+e}_B$. The specified base-change identifications identify its source with $D_d\otimes^LD_e$, its pulled-back $\sigma$ with $\nu_{d,e}$, and $Lz_{d+e}^*Lq^*G_g^{-1}$ with $b_e$. The rank-$d$ bundle is the base change of $P_d$, so its pulled-back inverse orientation is $b_d$. Monoidality and Tate pullback identify the pulled-back $\mu$ with the same concatenation on $B$. Consequently
$$b_{d+e}\nu_{d,e}=\mu(b_d\otimes b_e).$$
The vector-integration comparison identifies the inverse integration-transposed map with the bundle orientation used in the chart lemma. Therefore, in each actual normal-bundle frame, $\beta_f=b_d$, $Lf^*\beta_g=b_e$ and $\beta_{gf}=b_{d+e}$. The rank-zero formula follows from the unit calculation in Step 4.
